statement: Are there infinitely many $n$ such that, for all $k\geq 1$,\[\tau(n+k)\ll k?\]
remarks:
A stronger form of [248].

Lau \cite{La26} has proved that there exists an absolute constant $C$ such that, for infinitely many $n$,\[\tau(n+k) \ll k^C\]for all $k\geq 1$.
references: [La26] C. F. Lau, On the number of prime factors of consecutive integers. arXiv:2604.15042 (2026).
